# TAX PARTNER MEMORANDUM
## Deal Structure, Elections & Post-Closing Tax Step-Plan
**Matter:** Project Atlas – Proposed Acquisition
**Date:** October 3, 2026
**Prepared by:** Tax Partner (Advisory)
**Status:** DRAFT – FOR DISCUSSION

---

## PART I — EXECUTIVE SUMMARY & STRUCTURE SELECTION

### 1.1 Transaction Overview (Assumed Facts)

For purposes of this memorandum, we assume the following transaction parameters pending receipt of definitive deal documents:

| Parameter | Assumed Value |
|---|---|
| Target | Atlas Operating Co., LLC (taxed as S-Corp via check-the-box election) |
| Seller | Founding shareholders (3 individuals) + Institutional PE Sponsor (1 fund) |
| Buyer | Acquiror, Inc. (C-Corp, publicly traded) |
| Enterprise Value | $250,000,000 |
| Rollover Equity | 15% of post-close equity (~$37,500,000) |
| Earnout | Up to $25,000,000 over 24-month period |
| Closing Target Date | December 31, 2026 |
| Escrow Holdback | $12,500,000 (18-month general rep & warranty escrow) |

*All figures and facts should be confirmed against the executed Letter of Intent and final disclosure schedules before relying on this memorandum.*

---

### 1.2 Structure Selection Matrix

We evaluated three primary acquisition structures. The analysis below drives our recommended structure.

#### TAX-PROV-1
**Asset Purchase vs. Stock Purchase vs. Statutory Merger — Comparative Analysis**

| Factor | Asset Purchase | Stock Purchase | Forward Triangular Merger |
|---|---|---|---|
| Step-up in basis | Full step-up on all acquired assets | No step-up (absent §338 election) | No step-up (absent §338(h)(10)) |
| Buyer preference | High — maximizes depreciation/amortization | Neutral without election | Neutral without election |
| Seller preference | Low — ordinary income on §1245/§1250 recapture; double tax risk for C-Corp sellers | High — capital gains at entity or shareholder level | High — potential tax-free reorganization treatment |
| Contingent liabilities | Buyer generally avoids unknown liabilities | Buyer assumes all | Buyer assumes all |
| Transfer taxes | May trigger state/local transfer taxes on real property | Typically no transfer taxes | Typically no transfer taxes |
| Consent requirements | May require third-party consents for asset transfers | Minimal consents (change of control provisions only) | Moderate — plan of merger filing requirements |
| Rollover mechanics | More complex; requires new entity | Straightforward — sellers retain equity | Straightforward — exchange of shares |

**Recommended Structure: Forward Triangular Merger with §338(h)(10) Election**

Given that:
(a) Target is an S-Corporation (eligible for §338(h)(10));
(b) Buyer desires a stepped-up asset basis for depreciation/amortization of goodwill and intangibles (estimated 15-year §197 amortization stream);
(c) Sellers seek to preserve capital gains treatment on the bulk of proceeds;
(d) Rollover equity is material (15%) and must be structured to avoid immediate gain recognition;

we recommend a **Forward Triangular Merger** of Target into a newly formed Merger Sub (wholly owned by Acquiror, Inc.), followed by a **joint §338(h)(10) election** by the S-Corporation shareholders and Acquiror.

---

## PART II — ELECTIONS

### 2.1 Section 338(h)(10) Election

#### TAX-PROV-2
**§338(h)(10) Election Mechanics and Requirements**

A valid §338(h)(10) election requires:
1. Target must be a domestic corporation that is either (i) a member of a consolidated group, (ii) a member of an affiliated group that files separate returns, or (iii) an **S-Corporation** ← *applies here*;
2. Acquiror must make a "qualified stock purchase" (QSP) — acquisition of at least 80% of total voting power and value within a 12-month acquisition period;
3. Election must be made jointly on IRS Form 8023 no later than the **15th day of the 9th month** beginning after the month in which the acquisition date falls (i.e., for a December 31, 2026 close, deadline is **September 15, 2027**);
4. All S-Corporation shareholders must consent; the PE sponsor's consent mechanics must be confirmed under its fund documents.

**Tax Effect of Election:**
- Target is treated as having sold all its assets in a single deemed asset sale on the acquisition date at aggregate deemed sale price (ADSP);
- ADSP = Grossed-up amount realized by selling shareholders + Target liabilities assumed;
- Target's S-Corp status terminates on the acquisition date; any built-in gains tax exposure under §1374 is accelerated to the deemed sale;
- Sellers recognize gain/loss as if they sold assets (pass-through character) → reported on individual returns for the final S-Corp short-year;
- Buyer receives a stepped-up cost basis in all Target assets allocated under §1060 / Treas. Reg. §1.338-6.

**Estimated Amortization Benefit to Buyer:**
Assuming ~$180M allocated to §197 intangibles (goodwill, customer relationships, non-compete agreements), the annual amortization deduction is **$12,000,000/year** for 15 years, generating an estimated NPV tax benefit of ~$34M–$40M at a 21% federal rate (discounted at 8%).

#### TAX-PROV-3
**Allocation of Aggregate Deemed Sale Price — §1060 / §338 Residual Method**

Asset classes under Treas. Reg. §1.338-6(b):

| Class | Asset Type | Estimated Allocation |
|---|---|---|
| I | Cash & cash equivalents | $2,500,000 |
| II | Actively traded personal property; CDs; government securities | $1,200,000 |
| III | Accounts receivable; mortgages; credit card receivables | $8,300,000 |
| IV | Inventory | $4,000,000 |
| V | All other tangible assets (PP&E) | $22,000,000 |
| VI | §197 intangibles (other than goodwill/going concern) | $32,000,000 |
| VII | Goodwill and going-concern value (residual) | $148,000,000 |
| **Total** | | **$218,000,000** |

*Note: ADSP will exceed closing cash consideration by the amount of assumed liabilities. Allocation schedule must be agreed between Buyer and Seller and attached as a closing deliverable. Both parties are required to file Form 8594; allocations must be consistent.*

#### TAX-PROV-4
**Check-the-Box and S-Corp Termination Elections**

- No new check-the-box election is required for the merger itself; however, if Buyer elects to operate Target as a disregarded entity post-close, a Form 8832 election (effective date = day after acquisition date) should be filed within 75 days of close.
- Buyer should confirm whether it prefers (i) disregarded entity (simplest — assets/liabilities reported on Acquiror's consolidated return), (ii) qualified subchapter S subsidiary (Q-Sub) — *not available post-acquisition by C-Corp*, or (iii) C-Corp subsidiary.
- **Recommended:** Convert to disregarded entity via Form 8832 on Day 1 to eliminate separate return filing obligations, simplify intercompany eliminations, and allow immediate use of Target's net operating losses (subject to §382 limitations — see TAX-PROV-7).

#### TAX-PROV-5
**State and Local Tax Elections**

| State | Issue | Required Election / Action |
|---|---|---|
| Delaware | Merger filing | File Certificate of Merger with DE Secretary of State on closing date |
| [Target's principal state] | Combined/consolidated reporting | Evaluate unitary filing group inclusion; file amended election within 30 days of close if required |
| [Target's principal state] | State §338 equivalents | Many states do not automatically conform to federal §338(h)(10); separate state elections or forms may be required |
| All nexus states | Change-of-control registration | File for authority to do business in new name; update registered agent information |

*Nexus review to be completed within 30 days of signing; state conformity memo to follow.*

### 2.2 Additional Elections

#### TAX-PROV-6
**Taxable Year Election**

Post-close, Acquiror's consolidated group uses a calendar year. Target's final S-Corp short year runs January 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026 (the acquisition date). Sellers must file a final S-Corp return (Form 1120-S) for this short year. Buyer's Merger Sub will be included in the consolidated return from the acquisition date forward.

If close occurs before December 31, 2026, an interim closing of the books election should be made under §1362(e)(6) to allocate S-Corp income/deductions between the S-Short Year and the C-Short Year based on actual results rather than pro-ration. **We strongly recommend this election** given likely acceleration of year-end income.

#### TAX-PROV-7
**§382 NOL Limitation Analysis**

Post-acquisition, any pre-change NOLs carried forward by Target are subject to the annual §382 limitation:
- Annual §382 Limit = Value of Target's stock immediately before the ownership change × long-term tax-exempt rate (published monthly by IRS; current rate ~3.4%);
- Estimated limit ≈ $250M × 3.4% = **$8,500,000/year**;
- Confirm Target's NOL balance on closing date; given §338(h)(10) deemed asset sale treatment, pre-close NOLs are generally absorbed in the deemed sale — this should be modeled in the waterfall.

## PART III — ROLLOVER EQUITY MECHANICS

#### TAX-PROV-8
**Rollover Equity — Avoiding Gain Recognition at Close**

The 15% rollover (estimated $37,500,000) by selling shareholders must be structured to defer gain recognition. Two primary approaches:

**Option A: Direct Rollover into Acquiror Stock (Reorganization Treatment)**
- If the overall transaction qualifies as a reorganization under §368(a)(2)(D) (forward triangular merger), shareholders who receive solely Acquiror stock (no boot) recognize no gain.
- Shareholders who receive a mix of cash and stock must recognize gain (but not loss) to the extent of boot received (§356).
- **Trap:** The 15% rollover shareholders receiving Acquiror stock must hold for at least 1 year to achieve long-term capital gains rates on future sale.
- **Continuity of Interest:** At least 40% of total consideration must be Acquiror stock for reorganization qualification; at 15% rollover on $250M deal ($37.5M stock / $250M total = 15%) — **this does not meet the 40% COI threshold.** Reorganization treatment is **not available** under these facts.

**Option B: Rollover into NewCo/HoldCo Equity (Recommended)**
- Establish a new HoldCo entity (taxed as a partnership or LLC) into which rolling shareholders contribute their Target equity in exchange for HoldCo equity units immediately before close;
- The merger then occurs at the Target level; HoldCo receives the merger consideration (cash for 85%; HoldCo equity interests in Acquiror sub for 15%);
- Rolling shareholders' contribution to HoldCo is analyzed under §721 (partnership contribution — generally non-recognition) or §351 (if HoldCo is a corporation);
- **Recommended HoldCo structure:** Partnership (LLC taxed as partnership) to allow flexible profit/loss allocations, promote structures for management rollover participants, and avoid double-tax on future distributions.

**Gain Recognition Risk:**
- If HoldCo is a partnership, rolling shareholders should receive no gain recognition on the exchange if properly documented as a partnership contribution under §721, provided no disguised sale rules apply (§707(a)(2)(B)).
- **Disguised Sale Risk:** If HoldCo distributes cash to rolling shareholders within 2 years of formation, the IRS may recharacterize the contribution as a disguised sale. Structure distributions carefully; maintain 2-year holding period documentation.

#### TAX-PROV-9
**Rollover Equity — HoldCo Operating Agreement Tax Provisions**

The HoldCo LLC Agreement must include:
1. **Capital Account Maintenance:** Capital accounts maintained in accordance with Treas. Reg. §1.704-1(b)(2)(iv);
2. **Substantial Economic Effect:** Liquidation proceeds distributed in accordance with positive capital account balances;
3. **Deficit Restoration Obligations or Qualified Income Offset:** At least one must be included;
4. **Tax Distribution Rights:** Quarterly tax distributions equal to each member's allocable share of taxable income × assumed combined federal/state rate (suggested: 45%) to ensure members can pay taxes on pass-through income;
5. **Anti-Dilution Protections:** Pre-emptive rights on new issuances to protect rollover percentage;
6. **Put/Call Provisions:** Rolling shareholders should have a put right (at Fair Market Value) exercisable after 3 years; Buyer should have a call right exercisable after 5 years or upon liquidity event.

## PART IV — EARNOUT MECHANICS

#### TAX-PROV-10
**Earnout Structure — Tax Characterization**

The $25,000,000 earnout is payable over 24 months. Tax treatment depends on characterization:

| Scenario | Tax Treatment to Seller | Tax Treatment to Buyer |
|---|---|---|
| Earnout is additional purchase price (not compensation) | Capital gain when received (installment sale rules may apply under §453) | Added to basis; amortizable over §197 life if allocated to intangibles |
| Earnout is compensation (seller-employees remain employed) | Ordinary income | Deductible in year paid (subject to §162) |
| Mixed earnout (part purchase price, part compensation) | Bifurcated treatment | Bifurcated treatment |

**Key Risk — §83 / Golden Parachute:** If selling shareholders are also employees post-close and earnout receipt is conditioned on continued employment, the IRS will likely recharacterize as compensation. **Recommendation:** Ensure earnout agreement explicitly states payments are not contingent on continued employment and are tied solely to business performance metrics.

#### TAX-PROV-11
**Earnout — Installment Sale Treatment**

If earnout is treated as additional purchase price:
- Sellers may elect installment sale treatment under §453 to defer gain recognition to the year earnout payments are received;
- The gross profit percentage (GPP) is applied to each payment received;
- **Election:** Installment method is the default for qualifying sales; seller must **opt out** on a timely filed return if immediate recognition is preferred;
- **Installment Sale Obligation Interest:** Imputed interest rules under §483 / §1274 apply if the stated rate is below the Applicable Federal Rate (AFR). Current AFR (long-term, semi-annual compounding, October 2026): ~4.15%. Earnout agreement should specify interest at or above AFR to avoid imputed interest recharacterization.
- **§453A Interest Charge:** If deferred installment obligations exceed $5,000,000, sellers are subject to an interest charge on the deferred tax liability. At $25M earnout, this is a significant concern; model the §453A charge against the time-value benefit of deferral.

#### TAX-PROV-12
**Earnout Metrics — Validation Framework**

Earnout is proposed based on EBITDA targets over 24 months. The following validation checkpoints are required:

**Metric Definition Risks:**
- EBITDA must be defined consistently with the acquisition-date accounting methodology; specify:
  - Treatment of purchase accounting adjustments (depreciation step-up, amortization of intangibles should be **excluded** from earnout EBITDA calculation to avoid Buyer penalizing Seller for its own allocation decisions);
  - Treatment of one-time/non-recurring items;
  - Treatment of new acquisitions by Buyer post-close (revenue/EBITDA from bolt-ons should be **excluded** from Target's earnout calculation);
  - Treatment of intercompany charges post-close (management fees, allocated overhead must be capped or excluded);
  - FX adjustments (if Target has international operations);

**Earnout Milestone Schedule (Assumed):**

| Period | EBITDA Target | Max Earnout Payment | Payment Date |
|---|---|---|---|
| Year 1 (Jan–Dec 2027) | $28,000,000 | $12,500,000 | March 31, 2028 |
| Year 2 (Jan–Dec 2028) | $32,000,000 | $12,500,000 | March 31, 2029 |
| **Total** | | **$25,000,000** | |

**Validation Requirements:**
1. Buyer must deliver an Earnout Statement within 60 days of each measurement period end;
2. Sellers have 30 days to object; disputes go to an agreed accounting firm neutral;
3. Tax partner to review draft Earnout Statements for consistency with purchase price allocation and tax return positions.

## PART VI — TAX REPRESENTATIONS & WARRANTIES (Summary)

#### TAX-PROV-13
**Key Tax Representations — Seller Obligations**

The following tax representations shall be made by Sellers in the purchase agreement (standard positions; to be negotiated):

1. Target has timely filed all Tax Returns required to be filed through the closing date (or validly extended);
2. All Taxes shown as due on such Tax Returns have been paid;
3. Target has maintained a valid S-Corporation election continuously since [inception/date]; no event has occurred that would terminate the S-Corp election;
4. Target has not been subject to a Tax audit within the last [3] years; no pending or threatened Tax audit, assessment, or deficiency;
5. Target has no liability for Taxes of any other person (no consolidated group liability, transferee liability, or contractual indemnity);
6. Target has withheld and paid all required employment taxes, backup withholding, and sales/use taxes;
7. No closing agreement or advance pricing agreement with any Taxing Authority is in effect;
8. Target has no §1374 built-in gains tax liability as of the closing date (subject to carve-out for amounts disclosed in the Disclosure Schedules);
9. The purchase price allocation set forth in the Allocation Schedule is consistent with the fair market values of the assets and with §1060.

#### TAX-PROV-14
**Tax Indemnification Covenants**

Sellers shall indemnify Buyer for:
1. All Taxes of Target for any Pre-Closing Tax Period (including the S-Corp short year);
2. All Taxes arising from a breach of any Tax representation;
3. All Taxes resulting from the §338(h)(10) deemed asset sale (except to the extent already reflected in the purchase price reduction);
4. Transfer Taxes (allocated 50%/50% per negotiation, or 100% Seller-borne — to be agreed);
5. Any §1374 built-in gains tax triggered by the deemed asset sale.

Buyer shall indemnify Sellers for all Taxes of Target for any Post-Closing Tax Period.

**Survival Period:** Tax representations and indemnities shall survive until 60 days after the expiration of the applicable statute of limitations (including extensions), which for federal income tax purposes is generally 3 years from the due date of the return (plus 6 years for substantial omission of income; no expiration for fraud).

#### TAX-PROV-15
**Tax Refund Provisions**

Any Tax refund attributable to a Pre-Closing Tax Period (including carrybacks of post-closing losses to pre-closing years, to the extent permitted) shall be for the account of Sellers, net of any reasonable out-of-pocket costs incurred by Buyer in obtaining such refund. Buyer shall promptly remit any such refund to Sellers within [15] business days of receipt. The parties acknowledge that Buyer shall not be required to carryback any post-closing Tax attributes to pre-closing periods, and shall not file amended returns for pre-closing periods without Sellers' consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) if such amended return would affect Sellers' Tax liability.

#### TAX-PROV-16
**Straddle Period Allocation**

To the extent any Tax period of Target begins before and ends after the closing date (a "Straddle Period"), Taxes shall be allocated between Pre-Closing and Post-Closing portions as follows:
- For income, gains, deductions, and losses: **interim closing of the books method** (per TAX-PROV-6 election);
- For real and personal property taxes and other periodic taxes not based on income: **pro-rata daily allocation**;
- For sales/use taxes and transaction-based taxes: **based on the period in which the underlying transaction occurred**.

#### TAX-PROV-17
**Tax Return Preparation and Control**

1. Sellers shall prepare (at their expense) all Tax Returns for Target for Pre-Closing Tax Periods, including the final S-Corp short-year return. Such returns shall be submitted to Buyer for review at least 30 days prior to filing; Buyer shall have 15 days to review and provide comments; Sellers shall incorporate Buyer's reasonable comments;
2. Buyer shall prepare all Tax Returns for Target for Post-Closing Tax Periods and Straddle Periods. Straddle Period returns shall be submitted to Sellers' representative for review 30 days prior to filing; Sellers shall have 15 days to review;
3. Buyer shall control all Tax audits for Post-Closing periods; Sellers shall control Pre-Closing Tax audits (subject to Buyer's right to participate at its own expense);
4. Neither party shall amend any Tax Return for a Pre-Closing Tax Period without the other party's prior written consent (not to be unreasonably withheld).
